statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases from 24 to 21 as the 30,531.00 low holds a second hour and NVDA turns positive pre-market, while Stress edges down to 83 and stays in the extreme band.
recommendation: The overnight extension sequence has now failed to resume for two consecutive hours. NQ has made no new low since 09:00Z, has recovered 88.50 points from 30,531.00 to 30,619.50 and has narrowed its decline from -1.02% to -0.87%. A fresh company-level catalyst has also arrived inside this clock-hour: NVIDIA disclosed a $150 billion increase to its repurchase authorisation, taking the total to $235 billion through fiscal 2028, and NVDA is quoted +1.10% pre-market at 227.54 having been -0.36% an hour ago. The largest Nasdaq-100 weight moving against the AI-capex-slowdown narrative is the single clearest non-confirmation of a persistent one-way path, and it sits alongside a DAX still flat at -0.05%, a VIX at 16.36 that has slipped off its 16.43 session high, a 10-year at 5.22% after touching 5.24%, and WTI at 95.68 after a 96.54 high. Every amplifier is a fraction off its extreme rather than extending. Tail therefore eases to 21 and the mapped policy state remains WATCH. It is not published lower because the backdrop is unresolved rather than repaired: the 10-year is still near its highest since 2007, WTI is still up 3.54% on a Strait of Hormuz standoff in which talks and strikes both remain possible, gold is still down 3.15%, META is -3.02% pre-market, and the OpenAI training pause leaves the AI-capex question open into the U.S. session. The published forecast therefore still carries Tail into the elevated band from 13:00Z to 15:00Z and keeps the danger window at 13:00Z to 16:00Z. A fresh break of 30,531.00 that extends without a meaningful retracement would be the observation that carries Tail back above the watch band.
headline: NQ recovers 88.50 points to 30,619.50 at -0.87% with the 30,531.00 low intact for two hours, and NVDA turns +1.10% pre-market on a $150bn buyback, easing Tail to 21 while Stress edges to 83
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 30,619.50 on the 11:18Z Yahoo Finance quote and 30,619.00 on the 11:17Z Investing.com quote, 269.75 and 270.25 points or 0.87% below Friday's 30,889.25 settlement. Both feeds report an unchanged session low of 30,531.00 and Yahoo Finance keeps the Globex high at 30,920.75 for a 389.75-point range. Investing.com's narrower calendar-day range of 30,531.00 to 30,705.50 places current price in the upper half of today's trade.

The structural picture has improved for a second consecutive hour. The 30,531.00 low was set before 09:00Z and has now survived two full clock-hours, price has recovered 88.50 points from it, and the decline against settlement has narrowed from 1.02% to 0.87%. Repeated extension after a failed retracement is the observed structure the Tail score exists to flag; it drove Tail to 26 at 09:00Z, was absent at 10:00Z and remains absent now, with a retracement of real size in its place. Tail accordingly eases to 21 within the watch band.

The decisive new evidence this hour is company-level. NVIDIA disclosed a $150 billion increase to its share repurchase authorisation, lifting the total available to $235 billion through fiscal 2028, the largest such increase in its history against the $50 billion added a year ago. NVDA is quoted at 227.54 pre-market, +1.10%, and reported up 1.9% in Monday morning trade, having been -0.36% at the previous assessment. That matters because the overnight decline was transmitted through the AI-capex channel: SK Hynix fell 4.8% and Samsung Electronics 4.6% in Asia after OpenAI paused training, evaluation and inference with tool use for its most capable models pending a safety review. The largest index constituent now trading higher on its own catalyst directly weakens the mechanism by which that narrative would produce a persistent one-way Nasdaq-100 path.

The remaining megacap and cross-asset evidence is mixed rather than aligned, which is the condition under which Tail stays contained. MSFT is -0.46% pre-market at 513.79 and META is -3.02% at 728.95, so index-level pressure is concentrated rather than broad. The DAX is 25,395.49, -0.05%, within a 25,360.32 to 25,508.57 range, still withholding confirmation of a 0.87% NQ decline. The VIX is 16.36, up 10.02% from Friday's 14.87 close but below its 16.43 session high, the first intraday decay observed today. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.22%, up about 6 basis points, off the 5.24% recorded an hour ago, with the 2-year at 4.92%, the 5-year at 5.06% and the 30-year at 5.53%. WTI is 95.68, up 3.54% after a 96.54 high, and Brent is 100.72, up 3.37% within a 97.63 to 101.24 range; two secondary reports quoted Brent near 107 to 108, and that divergence is treated as a contract or data inconsistency rather than a price, since the direct futures quote and the WTI level agree with each other. Gold remains the clearest read on the character of the move, down 3.15% to 4,185.10 from a 4,315.60 high: falling gold alongside falling equities and rising yields identifies a real-rate repricing rather than a flight to safety, and that class of move has historically produced two-sided, retracing equity paths.

Stress eases marginally to 83 and stays in the extreme band. Every amplifier has come a small distance off its extreme, but none has resolved: oil is still up more than 3% on both benchmarks on an unresolved Strait of Hormuz standoff, the 10-year is still near its highest since 2007, gold has still lost more than 3%, and the week ahead carries ADP, Core PCE, Personal Spending and final Q2 GDP on Wednesday, ISM Manufacturing on Thursday and Non-Farm Payrolls on Friday, with quarter-end rebalancing on 30 September and JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence tomorrow. That is a genuinely difficult, high-volatility environment in which a large but recoverable drawdown is plausible, and it can coexist with Tail below the blocking threshold.

Confidence rises to 87. Two independent NQ feeds agree on price, change and the session low; the full yield curve, the VIX, gold and both oil benchmarks are current; the DAX and three megacap pre-market quotes are live; and the new NVIDIA authorisation, the OpenAI pause and the Iran position are each verified against dated reporting. Confidence is held below 90 because of the conflicting Brent prints and because the shared Finviz context carried a 05:58Z collection time, roughly five and a half hours old with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so only its latest-session breadth and megacap tone were usable as non-real-time background and nothing in it established current NQ structure.

On Iran, President Trump rejected Tehran's seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on 26 September, saying the conditions might have been acceptable a year ago, while indicating he expects negotiations to resume this week; Iran's foreign minister said Tehran is prepared for both diplomacy and confrontation. A catalyst that can resolve in either direction raises the volatility environment measured by Stress and the event-path uncertainty in the published forecast, and it does not by itself establish the directional efficiency that Tail measures.

The published danger window is unchanged at 13:00Z to 16:00Z, covering the 13:30Z cash open, the post-open continuation window and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release. That is where an aligned opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would supply the observation needed to carry Tail back into the elevated band. A fresh break of 30,531.00 that extends without a meaningful retracement, a reversal of the NVDA bid at the open, or a European close that finally confirms the overnight direction would be the invalidations of the present reading.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail held at 7-8% through the Sunday European and U.S. hours, drifted from 9% to 14% across the Globex reopen as Stress climbed from 63% to 76%, eased to 9-12% between 00:00Z and 02:00Z, then stepped to 21% at 03:00Z when NQ first took out Friday's low, 22% at 04:00Z, 21% at 05:00Z and 24% for the three hours from 06:00Z to 08:00Z as successive overnight lows broke, crossed to 26% at 09:00Z on a failed retracement and returned to 24% at 10:00Z once that extension stalled. Stress rose almost monotonically from 63% to 85% and Confidence from 70% to 86%. Dominant mode was normal for sixteen hours, mixed at 02:00Z, 05:00Z and 10:00Z and trend-down at 03:00Z, 04:00Z and for the four hours from 06:00Z to 09:00Z. Sixteen hours mapped to EA_ON, seven to WATCH and the 09:00Z hour to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES.
outlookSummary: The published horizon runs from the 11:00Z hour on 28 September through 10:00Z on 29 September. Tail opens at 21% in the watch band and enters the 25-34 elevated band for only three hours, 13:00Z to 15:00Z, peaking at 27% on the 14:00Z hour that covers post-open continuation risk and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release. It returns to the watch band from 16:00Z, drifts between 20% and 23% through the Asian and European sessions with a local high of 23% on the 01:00Z hour when China and Korea reprice the AI-capex question against the new NVIDIA buyback for a second session, and falls to 17% in the low band only for the 21:00Z CME maintenance halt, when no meaningful price discovery exists. Stress eases from 83% to 78% and back to 80%, staying in the high-to-extreme range, reflecting WTI up 3.54%, a 10-year yield near its highest since 2007, gold down 3.15% and a week carrying JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence on Tuesday, ADP, Core PCE and final Q2 GDP on Wednesday, ISM Manufacturing on Thursday and Non-Farm Payrolls on Friday alongside quarter-end rebalancing. Confidence decays from 87% to 61% with distance from the evidence cutoff. Only the 11:00Z hour states observed price-path structure as current fact; every later hour states its structure conditionally, as a checkpoint, assumption or invalidation.
